description.value: Built in 1896 during the Salmo River Valley mining boom, Hotel Ymir is one of the oldest surviving buildings in the West Kootenay region and has been fully restored as a country resort with a licensed dining room (Pau Hana), a lounge (Cowichan), and a remarkable world art collection. The hotel sits directly across from the old Burlington Northern Railway corridor, now a 50+ km converted rail trail ideal for hiking and cycling along the Salmo River. Accommodation ranges from hostel-style bunk rooms on the third floor to en-suite queen rooms and two suites with gas fireplaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is accessible and corroborates all OSM contact details (phone 250-357-9611, address 7104 1st Ave, Ymir BC). The accommodations page explicitly states 'High speed wireless internet access is available throughout the hotel,' and the front page confirms on-site licensed dining (Pau Hana Dining Room and Cowichan Lounge). No mention of bike storage, staff bike procedures, laundry, e-bike charging, tools, or most other cycling amenities anywhere on the site.
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Nelson' but the hotel is physically located in Ymir, BC (V0G 2K0), a separate community roughly 50 km south of Nelson.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, operational historic hotel on a major cycling rail trail corridor with on-site food and Wi-Fi — clearly useful to touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: The Burlington Northern Railway Trail, a 50+ km converted rail trail running along the Salmo River past the hotel, is likely of strong interest to touring cyclists and gravel riders.

Nearby evening food.detail: On-site licensed Pau Hana Dining Room and Cowichan Lounge, described as offering food and drink service
